question: Can the 2021 Liguasan Marsh gut-content paper support a verified, taxon-specific natural-diet note in Bangwit?

source.citation: Fabay, R. V., Alejos, M. S., and Fabay, J. V. (2021). Gut Content Analysis of Freshwater Fishes from Liguasan Marsh, Maguindanao. Uttar Pradesh Journal of Zoology, 42(23), 227-232. https://www.mbimph.com/index.php/UPJOZ/article/view/2635

metadataOnly.publisherAbstractClaim: The abstract says the study examined gut contents of eight common freshwater fishes from Liguasan Marsh and reports five broad feeding guilds: algae, fish, crustaceans, detritus and mollusks. It says algal feeders were most represented and detritus and mollusk feeders were each represented by one species.
metadataOnly.detailLimit: The accessible publisher abstract does not identify which named taxon consumed which food category, sample counts, field dates, collection locations or identification confidence. It cannot support species-specific diet cards by itself.

accessAudit.publisherFullTextAttempt: A normal request to the publisher's linked PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. No access control, login, or challenge was bypassed.
accessAudit.siteFooterObservation: The publisher landing page footer states that the journal site is copyright and all rights reserved; this does not establish an item-specific reuse license for the article.

interpretation.safeSummary: The publisher abstract supports only a broad study-level statement that eight freshwater fishes were grouped into five feeding guilds, with algal feeders most represented. The full article could not be retrieved from its publisher in this review, so no taxon-by-food mapping or sample-level result was verified.
notSupported: A named species' prey or food list based on the abstract alone.
A universal or nationwide diet rule for dalag, tilapia, or any other fish.
Fishing bait, lure, catchability, or guaranteed response advice.
Current presence, abundance, a full marsh inventory, or a capture-site map.
Public reproduction or adaptation of article content without verified item-specific terms.

qualityAndRights.evidenceLevel: Publisher metadata and abstract only; the primary article body, methods, tables and figures were not reviewed.
qualityAndRights.reuseStatus: No item-specific article license was verified. The publisher site footer says all rights reserved. No public-app reuse is approved.
qualityAndRights.handling: Only the citation, accessible abstract-level scope and access outcome are summarized. No full text, table, diet mapping, taxon row or image is retained.
qualityAndRights.dietBoundary: Abstract-level feeding-guild coverage is not a species-level prey observation and is not bait advice.

disposition.reason: The publisher PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403, the publisher abstract does not provide taxon-specific diet mappings, and no item-specific reuse license was found.

nextAction: Retry only through a normally available publisher, author, or institutional repository copy and verify its reuse terms. Until then, do not add taxon-specific diet details from this paper.

sources.supports: Publisher citation metadata, publication date, pagination, authors and abstract-level scope; landing page footer states the site is all rights reserved.
Publisher-linked full-text endpoint; a normal retrieval attempt returned HTTP 403 and the article body was not accessed.
Independent NFRDI bibliography citation of the Fabay et al. 2021 gut-content article.
